items.followUp: For which work did Melvin Calvin receive the Nobel Prize, and in what year?

rubric.why: Identifies the work for which Calvin was honoured.
rubric.description: Awarded for research on carbon dioxide fixation in photosynthesis, including the Calvin cycle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying this research.

rubric.why: Identifies the prize and its field.
rubric.description: He received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1961.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

modelAnswer: Melvin Calvin was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1961.
He received it for his research on carbon dioxide fixation in photosynthesis, which explained the Calvin cycle.

items.followUp: Expand NAD and state its role in cellular respiration.

rubric.why: Checks the full form of FAD.
rubric.description: FAD stands for flavin adenine dinucleotide.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct full form of FAD.

rubric.why: Checks the full form of NAD.
rubric.description: NAD stands for nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct full form of NAD.

modelAnswer: FAD stands for flavin adenine dinucleotide.
NAD stands for nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide.
Both are coenzymes that carry hydrogen/electrons during cellular respiration.

items.followUp: What is dietary fibre, and how does it help the digestive system?

rubric.why: Checks the definition of dietary fibre.
rubric.description: Dietary fibre is the indigestible part of plant food, such as cellulose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining fibre as indigestible plant material.

rubric.why: Checks a key benefit of fibre.
rubric.description: It adds bulk to food and helps bowel movement, preventing constipation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct digestive benefit.

modelAnswer: Dietary fibre is the indigestible part of plant food, such as cellulose.
It adds bulk to food and helps peristalsis, preventing constipation.

items.followUp: Define source and sink in the translocation of food in plants.

rubric.why: Checks understanding of the source in food transport.
rubric.description: A source is a plant part that produces or releases food, commonly a mature leaf.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing a source.

rubric.why: Checks understanding of the sink in food transport.
rubric.description: A sink is a plant part that uses or stores food, such as a root, fruit, or growing region.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing a sink.

modelAnswer: A source is a plant part that produces or releases food, usually a mature leaf.
A sink is a plant part that uses or stores food, such as a root, fruit, or growing region.

items.followUp: Name two ways in which white blood cells protect the body.

rubric.why: Checks one major defence function of white blood cells.
rubric.description: Some white blood cells engulf and destroy pathogens by phagocytosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for phagocytosis or an equivalent description.

rubric.description: Some white blood cells produce antibodies against pathogens.

modelAnswer: Some white blood cells engulf and destroy pathogens by phagocytosis.
Other white blood cells produce antibodies that help defend the body against pathogens.

items.followUp: State the main functions of xylem and phloem in plants.

rubric.why: Checks the transport function of xylem.
rubric.description: Xylem transports water and mineral salts from the roots to the rest of the plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating xylem's transport role.

rubric.why: Checks the transport function of phloem.
rubric.description: Phloem transports food, such as sugars, from sources to the parts that use or store it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating phloem's transport role.

modelAnswer: Xylem transports water and mineral salts from the roots to the rest of the plant.
Phloem transports food, such as sugars, from sources to the parts that use or store it.

items.followUp: Give one example each of how Biology is linked with Physics and Chemistry.

rubric.why: Checks a valid link between Biology and Physics.
rubric.description: Physics contributes principles and instruments used in Biology, such as the microscope.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example or explanation of the link.

rubric.why: Checks the link between Biology and Chemistry.
rubric.description: Chemistry helps explain the chemical composition of living things and their reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example or explanation of the link.

rubric.why: Checks the link between Biology and Mathematics.
rubric.description: Mathematics is used for measurements, calculations, and statistical analysis of biological data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example or explanation of the link.

rubric.why: Checks the link between Biology and Economics.
rubric.description: Biology supports economic activities through agriculture, livestock, fisheries, and biological industries.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example or explanation of the link.

modelAnswer: Biology and Physics: Physics provides instruments and principles used in Biology, such as the microscope and the study of energy in living systems.
Biology and Chemistry: Chemistry explains the chemical composition of organisms and the reactions that occur in them.
Biology and Mathematics: Mathematics is used to measure, calculate, and analyse biological data statistically.
Biology and Economics: Biological knowledge supports economic activities such as agriculture, livestock, fisheries, and biological industries.

items.followUp: What is enzyme specificity? Explain it with one example.

rubric.why: Checks the basis of substrate specificity.
rubric.description: An enzyme's active site fits a particular substrate, so the enzyme acts on that substrate specifically.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks: 1 for stating that enzymes are substrate-specific and 1 for linking this to the active site's fit.

rubric.why: Checks that enzyme action is specific to a reaction, with a valid example.
rubric.description: Each enzyme catalyses a particular reaction; for example, sucrase acts on sucrose.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks: 1 for stating reaction specificity and 1 for a correct example.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are specific: each enzyme acts on a particular substrate because its active site fits that substrate.
An enzyme catalyses a particular reaction; for example, sucrase acts on sucrose.
